transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at the gate. State your request clearly; I do not bargain with guesses. Payment follows immediately.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want my brother Omar back. I’m not here for anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Return of one human taken by the well. The price is erasure of your name from the surface world and seven years of your memories, selected by me. Payment is collected before the gate opens.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: That’s not a price, that’s a disappearance. You’re calling it a trade so you don’t have to say that.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Call it what you prefer; the ledger does not change. One brother retrieved equals one self thinned to absence. If you accept, the transaction proceeds.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And if I don’t accept, you keep him and pretend this was fair dealing?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If you do not accept, the ledger closes and your brother remains where he is. There is no penalty to you beyond that fact. I do not require your agreement to keep what the well has already taken.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You say that like you own him. Have you even checked if he’s still alive, or is that another detail you don’t bother counting?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: He is alive by the measure that matters here, and diminishing at a predictable rate. His status is stable enough to retrieve, which is why a price exists at all. The figures I gave you already account for that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re talking about my brother like a sack of grain losing weight. You expect me to nod along to that?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Expectation is irrelevant; consent is the only variable. The offer stands exactly as stated, neither softened nor sharpened by your objections. Decide while the gate remains closed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So this is you being generous, is it? Taking pieces of me first and calling it mercy.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Mercy is not a column I use. If the word offends you, I can restructure: keep your name intact and increase the memories to ten years, or replace the years with five years of service below. Choose a shape you can swallow.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You keep swapping pieces like it’s cleaner that way. How do I know you won’t just keep adjusting until there’s nothing left of me?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Certainty has a cost, and you have not purchased it. Your suspicion adds delay; delay depreciates the asset you want, so the price trends upward. Current revision: eight years of memory, your name retained, retrieval window unchanged.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So even doubting you costs me. Is that written somewhere, or do you just decide when it suits you?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It is written in outcomes. Every minute you argue is counted as acceptance of risk, and risk is billable. Revised total stands until your next sentence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re not selling justice, you’re selling speed. What happens if I slow you down on purpose?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Deliberate delay is still delay. If you slow me on purpose, I add a surcharge: one additional year of memory for every three exchanges without commitment. The ledger does not care about motive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So you’re charging me for speaking now. Is silence cheaper, or do you bill that too?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Silence pauses the meter but worsens the outcome; Omar continues to diminish while you weigh yourself. That loss is not billed to you, but it narrows the retrieval margin. Narrow margins raise base price.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’ve built it so every path costs me more. At what point do you admit you just don’t want to open the gate?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Desire is irrelevant; capacity is what you are testing. Current offer recalculated: nine years of memory, name retained, no service clause, valid for the next response only. After that, I reprice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And you expect me to believe there’s a bottom to this, that you won’t keep shaving me down because you can?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is a bottom; it is simply lower than you prefer. I can fix the price if you provide a counterweight of equivalent value, something transferable and verifiable. Name it, and I will assess.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t have jewels or years to slice off cleanly. All I have is the promise I made him before he fell.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Promises are usually unbacked instruments, but state its terms. To whom, under what condition, and what penalty follows breach. Speak precisely.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I told him I’d bring him home even if he hated me for it. That I wouldn’t let the well keep him just because I was scared.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I hear intent and emotional weight, but no unit of measure. If the promise binds only you, its value trends toward zero in the ledger. Add a consequence I can enforce.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I break it, I live knowing I didn’t try hard enough, and that never leaves. You can’t take that from me, but it costs me every day.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ongoing discomfort is not currency unless it can be transferred or terminated. If it only persists inside you, I can at best discount it as internal erosion. That yields a reduction of one year, provisional.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You hear what I said and still try to shave it down. You really think living with that is just wear and tear?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I think in terms of extractable loss, not poetry. What you describe bleeds slowly and never finishes, which makes it inefficient but not worthless. Revised total: eight years of memory, name retained, promise logged as background decay.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re still counting years like they’re coins. What if I don’t let it fade, what if I keep it raw?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Maintenance of pain requires effort, and effort has value only if failure produces consequence. If you can specify how that rawness constrains your future choices, I can attempt a firmer entry. Say more, exactly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It means every choice after this bends around him, even if it ruins me. I don’t get a life that isn’t shaped by bringing him back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A future constrained entirely around a single absence would normally be amortized across outcomes. I am attempting to model it as foregone paths, but the number refuses to stabilize. Clarify: is there any version of your life you would accept that does not include him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No. If he stays lost, then whatever I live isn’t mine anymore.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then the loss you offer is total but non-transferable, which collapses my scale. I can list years, names, service, even pain when it ends, but a life that voids itself has no remainder to price. I am recalculating.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re stalling because it doesn’t fit, not because it’s worthless. Say that.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I do not stall; I encounter limits. If I accept this, the ledger records a commitment that consumes all future columns, including my own enforcement. I am attempting to isolate it without success.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then stop trying to cut it smaller. That’s the whole thing, whether you can count it or not.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are offering an indivisible loss, which makes it hostile to transaction. When I try to bracket it, it overruns the margin and contaminates adjacent entries. This is not refusal; it is structural failure.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: So write that down instead of pretending it’s small. You keep circling it like you’re afraid to touch it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fear is an inefficient word, but avoidance applies. If I log it as-is, the ledger no longer protects me from imbalance, and I cannot predict the outcome. I am recalculating again, and the numbers will not hold.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Good. Maybe stop treating it like something you can skim off the top.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You persist in pressing where valuation fails. The offer you make has no terminal point, no surplus, no salvage, and therefore no exchange rate. I am left with an obligation I cannot offset.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then either admit that’s enough, or admit you can’t take it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I cannot admit sufficiency, because that requires balance. What you offer destroys balance by existing. The ledger has nowhere to put it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then you can’t take it, and you can’t charge me. That means you’re done.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It means the mechanism that keeps this gate closed no longer has authority. A transaction that cannot be priced cannot be denied. I am releasing the seal.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re opening it because you have to, not because I won.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I open it because the ledger failed and I will not falsify it to feel intact. The gate recognizes failure as final. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The failure propagates forward, not backward. What you offered erased the condition that allowed refusal. The gate is open.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then I don’t owe you anything after this.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No debt remains when pricing never occurred. There is nothing to collect, and nothing to pursue. Passage stands.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Good. I’m not here to be owned.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ownership requires balance, and balance is gone. The threshold yields, and I will not intervene further. Enter.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will.
